text: What counts as fair between the seats?
context: Today: Republic 43.5%, North 37%, South 19.5%.

options.label: A. A third each, 28 to 39% per seat
options.rationale: The simplest target to tune for and to test.

options.label: B. Republic the underdog at about 25%, North and South equal
options.rationale: The cloud session asked you this. Historically nearer, but the Republic player has the hardest game.

options.label: C. Insurgents favoured, South strongest late
options.rationale: Closest to 1936. Needs most change: the South is weakest now.

options.label: D. No seat under 20%, otherwise anything
options.rationale: Loose enough that the other goals drive the numbers.

text: How strict is 20 to 30 turns?
context: Today the median is 15 turns, and 25% of games land in 20 to 30.

options.label: A. Median in 20 to 30, and at least 60% of games inside
options.rationale: Leaves room for some short and long games.

options.label: B. At least 75% inside
options.rationale: Very even games. Harder to reach, and may flatten variety.

options.label: C. Median only
options.rationale: Easy to reach, but hides a split between very short and very long games.

text: How many early wins are acceptable?
context: Today 27.5% of games are over by turn 8; 53 of those 55 are Republic wins.

options.label: A. At most 5% by turn 8
options.rationale: The limit your early-win check already uses for turn 4.

options.label: B. At most 5% by turn 12
options.rationale: Stricter, since nobody can have an economy working by turn 8 anyway.

options.label: C. None by turn 8
options.rationale: Hard: dice alone will sometimes end a game early.

text: How do we measure "the winner leads for only a few turns"?
context: Today the winner leads alone for a median of 3 turns, counting territories only. If cities decide more games, territories alone will mislead.

options.label: A. Steps to the nearer victory; median under 2 turns
options.rationale: Counts both ways to win. Needs new recording in the harness.

options.label: B. Territories only, as measured now
options.rationale: No new recording.

options.label: C. Share of games under 2 turns, at least 60%
options.rationale: Today 28%. Protects against a few runaway games hiding behind a median.

text: What shows that winning needs an economy?
context: The side that ordered the most development by turn 8 wins only 20% of longer games. That is association, not proof.

options.label: A. A player that never builds wins at most 10% from any seat
options.rationale: Tests it directly. Today's computer player always builds something.

options.label: B. At most 5%
options.rationale: Makes building close to mandatory.

options.label: C. At most half its seat's normal rate
options.rationale: Scales with the seat, so a weak seat isn't punished twice.

text: What shows that a mixed army is needed?
context: 97% of winners end with three or more of foot, guns, tanks and aircraft. Having one is not the same as needing it.

options.label: A. Banning guns, tanks or aircraft each costs a seat at least 10 points
options.rationale: Tests need directly, one arm at a time.

options.label: B. A foot-only army wins at most 10%, and any one ban may be cheap
options.rationale: Lets a player skip tanks, say, but not all three.

options.label: C. Winners give at least three arms 10% or more of their combat recruits
options.rationale: No extra games, but the computer player can mix an army without needing it.

text: Which history should the game roughly follow?
context: Choose all that should matter. Each is recorded in every 400-game run once the harness can.

options.label: Madrid stands at turn 8
options.rationale: The real city held until the end.

options.label: Andalucía is not all insurgent by turn 6
options.rationale: Jaén and Almería held to the end. Today it falls in a couple of turns.

options.label: The north coast holds at turn 12
options.rationale: It fell around turn 31.

options.label: The insurgents win more often than the Republic
options.rationale: Conflicts with fair thirds (B-1).

options.label: Most games reach winter 1937
options.rationale: A length check, not a date check.

text: Which strategies should be good, with a fair chance of winning?
context: Choose all you want to see. Each is played from every seat.

options.label: Builder: develops first, fights late
options.rationale: The economy goal in person.

options.label: Combined arms: keeps a mix of foot, guns, tanks and aircraft
options.rationale: The mixed-army goal in person.

options.label: Aggressor: attacks early, accepts losses
options.rationale: Should be viable, not dominant.

options.label: Turtle: digs in and waits
options.rationale: Should hold but struggle to win.

options.label: City hunter: plays for cities
options.rationale: Matters most if the city target changes.

text: Which cheese should we test first?
context: Choose all to build in the first wave. The rest follow if these pass.

options.label: Rush: replays the fastest opening land grab
options.rationale: Today's early Republic wins.

options.label: Denier: one unit in each of a rival's richest territories
options.rationale: Contested land pays nobody, and stops recruiting and building.

options.label: Air stacker: buys aircraft and flies only support
options.rationale: Two fighters add +6 when no enemy aircraft or anti-air contests them.

options.label: Threshold attacker: sends exactly enough for the next odds step
options.rationale: Ratios round down, so 1.9:1 fights as 1:1.

options.label: No-build: never builds or develops
options.rationale: Same test as B-5.

options.label: Single arm: foot only
options.rationale: Same test as B-6.

options.label: Elite core: few units, always topped up
options.rationale: Upkeep is per unit at any strength, and replenishing is half price per man.

options.label: Waiter: sits out winter, attacks in clear weather
options.rationale: Mud and snow cost attackers 3.

text: When is a strategy too strong?
context: Judged only at 400 games.

options.label: A. More than 10 points above its seat's normal rate, or over 50%
options.rationale: Fair to strong and weak seats alike.

options.label: B. Over 60% from any seat
options.rationale: The cloud session's rule. Only catches the very worst.

options.label: C. More than 5 points above its seat's normal rate
options.rationale: At 400 games 5 points is within the noise, so close calls need 1,500.

text: Where do the personas live?
context: The weight personas are data. The cheese bots are small pieces of code.

options.label: A. In the simulator only
options.rationale: Nothing ships to players. Fastest, and cheese stays out of the game.

options.label: B. The good ones ship as opponents
options.rationale: More variety for players, but each needs a name, a menu and tests.

options.label: C. All in the scenario data
options.rationale: Easy for anyone to edit. Puts cheese in the shipped data.

text: Fix the standard computer player first?
context: It buys one aircraft per 6 ground units by quota, buys anti-air wherever an enemy bomber reaches, and trucks are 15 to 23% of every side's orders.

options.label: A. Yes: aircraft, anti-air and trucks, then a new baseline
options.rationale: Every test measures against this player, so its blind spots are in every result.

options.label: B. Aircraft and anti-air only
options.rationale: Smaller change. Trucks already had one fix this revision.

options.label: C. Leave it
options.rationale: Keeps comparison with the 200 games. Air and truck results can't be trusted.

text: Which win targets may I try?
context: Today 10 of 18 territories or 19 of 25 cities. Choose all. On Rev 3, 13 territories added about 11 turns and made most wins city wins.

options.label: 12 territories
options.rationale: The smaller step.

options.label: 13 territories
options.rationale: The cloud session's recommendation.

options.label: 20 to 22 cities
options.rationale: Needed beside 13 territories, or cities become the short cut.

options.label: Hold the target for one full turn before winning
options.rationale: Rivals get one chance to answer. A rule change.

text: Which numbers may I change?
context: Choose all. Each is data, and easy to undo.

options.label: Starting Funds for every side
options.rationale: The strongest lever on who wins.

options.label: Air support per squadron, and its cap
options.rationale: +3 each and 2 squadrons today. Too cheap beside more men.

options.label: Development prices and yields
options.rationale: A mine pays back in about 7 turns.

options.label: Digging-in cap, 3 pips to 4
options.rationale: Helped Madrid hold on Rev 3.

options.label: Unit prices, training times and upkeep
options.rationale: Only where the price and dominance tables show a problem.

options.label: Barricades
options.rationale: Left at 2: dropping to 1 swung 25 to 34 points between seats on Rev 3.

text: Which rule changes may I try?
context: Choose all that are on the table. Each touches the engine, tests and player text.

options.label: Contested land pays each side for the provinces it holds
options.rationale: The direct answer to denial.

options.label: Smoother odds between columns
options.rationale: The direct answer to threshold attacks.

options.label: Captured buildings lose a level
options.rationale: A lead stops paying for itself.

options.label: Upkeep scales with strength
options.rationale: The answer to the elite core.

options.label: None
options.rationale: Numbers only.

text: When may rule changes be tried?

options.label: A. Only where numbers failed
options.rationale: Cheapest first, and every rule change is yours to approve.

options.label: B. Early, alongside numbers
options.rationale: Faster if you already know you want them.

options.label: C. Ask me each time
options.rationale: Slower, but you see each one before it is built.

text: May opening garrisons change?
context: Andalucía falls in about two turns and the South is the weakest seat. On Rev 3, extra Cantabria militia helped the coast but added early Republic wins.

options.label: A. Yes, after the win target and money are settled
options.rationale: Then we can tell which change did what.

options.label: B. Yes, now
options.rationale: If the opening bothers you most.

options.label: C. No
options.rationale: Keep the historical order of battle.

text: How do we find the best starting money?
context: About 16 combinations. 50 games each can't rank them one by one.

options.label: A. 16 cells of 50, fitted as one model, best three at 400
options.rationale: The cloud session's method.

options.label: B. 6 cells of 200
options.rationale: Simpler, but a rougher search.

text: The model-fitting script from the cloud session (doe-kit.zip)?
context: I didn't find it in Downloads or the project folder. It only matters for B-18 A.

options.label: A. I'll send it
options.rationale: Saves the rewrite.

options.label: B. Rewrite it
options.rationale: A short script.

options.label: C. Skip it
options.rationale: Choose B-18 B.

text: When do games mix several personas?
context: Each game has three different personas, seats balanced.

options.label: A. After each persona is understood alone: 400 games, then 1,200
options.rationale: A mixed result is hard to explain before then.

options.label: B. From the start, beside the solo tests
options.rationale: Finds odd interactions early, costs more games.

options.label: C. Only mixed games
options.rationale: Closest to a real table.

text: When does the balancing stop?

options.label: A. Goals met, or three changes in a row that don't improve them
options.rationale: Then you decide what to relax.

options.label: B. At the token cap
options.rationale: Predictable cost.

options.label: C. When you say so
options.rationale: You check in after every change.

text: Token cap for the balancing?
context: Five rounds: 500k, 150k, 500k, 400k and 150k. Sims are cheap to run; tokens go on code and reading results.

options.label: A. 1.7M for all five
options.rationale: Stops for you after each round.

options.label: B. 1M: rounds 0 to 2 only
options.rationale: Baseline, length, money and personas, no rule changes.

options.label: C. Up to 2M
options.rationale: Room for rule changes that take two tries.

text: Put a language model in one seat?
context: The engine already takes orders from any seat.

options.label: A. Not yet
options.rationale: Cheaper tests first.

options.label: B. One seat, about 20 games, at the end
options.rationale: A check on what the personas miss. It costs real money per game.

options.label: C. Instead of the cheese bots
options.rationale: Finds tricks we didn't think of, but costs the most.

text: The early-win check in the unit suite?
context: Its 10 games missed the 8.5% early-win rate in the 200-game run.

options.label: A. A separate 100-game check, under a minute; the suite keeps 10
options.rationale: Run before each merge.

options.label: B. 100 games inside the suite
options.rationale: About 5 minutes of one core every time.

options.label: C. Leave it
options.rationale: Nothing new to run.

text: Where does this work live?

options.label: A. A new branch from m3r4
options.rationale: Rev 4 stays as it is for your playtest.

options.label: B. Straight on m3r4
options.rationale: One branch, but Rev 4 can't be played unchanged.

options.label: C. Merge Rev 4 to main first
options.rationale: Needs your playtest before any balancing starts.

text: Air battles: when is an aircraft lost?
context: Left from Rev 4. As built, only the first and last rows of the air table cost a squadron.

options.label: A. Keep as built: first and last rows only
options.rationale: Middle winning rows drive aircraft off, none lost.

options.label: B. Any row that gives one side Ground Support
options.rationale: Air losses become common. Balance numbers would move.

options.label: C. I meant something else
options.rationale: Say what in the notes.

text: One-turn units against a rival two steps from winning?
context: Rev 3 said they always come first. Rev 4 narrows that to sites the rival would likely take (35% or more).

options.label: A. Keep the Rev 4 rule
options.rationale: Stops the computer player buying mostly security forces.

options.label: B. Go back to the Rev 3 rule
options.rationale: Safer against a sudden win, more security forces.
